text: Request for Examination (RFE) must be filed within 48 months from the priority date or filing date, whichever is earlier. If RFE is not filed within this period, the application is deemed to be withdrawn. There is NO extension possible for this deadline. The 48-month period is calculated from the earliest priority date if convention priority is claimed, otherwise from the Indian filing date.

First Examination Report (FER) response deadline: The applicant must respond to the FER within 6 months from the date of issuance. One extension of 3 months may be granted upon request and payment of extension fee before the original deadline expires. If no response is filed within the deadline (including any granted extension), the application is deemed to be abandoned.

Patent term in India is 20 years from the date of filing of the patent application. This is non-extendable. The term starts from the filing date, NOT the grant date. So if it takes 5 years to get a patent granted, you effectively have only 15 years of patent protection remaining. Patent term is the same for all types of inventions including pharmaceutical patents.

Convention priority period: If you first file a patent application in a Paris Convention country and want to file in India claiming that priority, you must file the Indian application within 12 months from the first filing date. This 12-month period is absolute and cannot be extended. Missing this deadline means you cannot claim the foreign priority date.

PCT (Patent Cooperation Treaty) national phase entry in India: The deadline is 31 months from the priority date. You can request entry into the national phase in India by filing Form 1 along with required documents and fees within this 31-month period. Late entry is not permitted. After national phase entry, the application is examined according to Indian patent law.

Patent renewal fees must be paid before the expiry of the second year from the date of the patent and every subsequent year. If not paid by the due date, a grace period of 6 months is available with surcharge. If renewal fee is not paid even within the grace period, the patent lapses. A lapsed patent can be restored within 18 months from the date of cessation by filing restoration petition with prescribed fee and showing sufficient cause for delay.

Pre-grant opposition can be filed by any person after publication of the application but before grant. There is no specific time limit for filing pre-grant opposition as long as the patent has not been granted. Opposition must be filed using Form 7A. The Controller may refuse to consider opposition filed close to the anticipated grant date.

Post-grant opposition must be filed within 12 months from the date of publication of grant of the patent. Only a 'person interested' can file post-grant opposition using Form 7. This is a strict deadline with no extension. Post-grant opposition is filed before the Opposition Board constituted by the Controller.
